strategy.thesis: Sonic Healthcare, one of the world's largest pathology/laboratory-medicine and diagnostic-imaging providers (ASX: SHL), makes direct strategic equity investments and forms joint ventures with AI-diagnostics startups to embed AI-assisted pathology and radiology reporting across its own lab and imaging network, rather than running an arms-length fund.

lifesci.science_platform_notes: Investment is paired with commercial deployment: Sonic's radiology AI (Annalise.ai, developed with Harrison.ai) is already used across Sonic's radiology division, and Franklin.ai (49% Sonic-owned directly, plus an indirect stake via Harrison.ai) is developing AI pathology products such as Prostate Digital for clinical evaluation in Sonic labs.

summary.en: Sonic Healthcare is an ASX-listed global pathology and diagnostic-imaging company that has taken direct equity stakes in AI-diagnostics startup Harrison.ai and co-created the AI pathology joint venture Franklin.ai, functioning as a corporate strategic investor in its own core diagnostics field.

sources.title: Harrison.ai raises AUD$129 million and partners with Sonic Healthcare

sources.quote: Harrison.ai raised AU$129 million in a Series B funding round led by Horizons Ventures, with new equity investment from Sonic Healthcare and I-MED Radiology Network.

verification_notes: Sonic Healthcare does not brand a named venture fund; its CVC-style activity documented here is limited to the Harrison.ai/Franklin.ai deal cluster found in company and press sources. No dedicated 'Sonic Ventures' unit could be verified.

strategy.thesis: Ramsay Health Care, one of the world's largest private-hospital operators (ASX: RHC), has made direct strategic equity investments into AI/digital-health startups such as Harrison.ai that can be deployed across its own hospital and diagnostic network, in addition to its core hospital operations.

summary.en: Ramsay Health Care is an ASX-listed private hospital operator that has made a direct venture-style equity investment in AI-diagnostics startup Harrison.ai, one of a very small number of externally-documented corporate venture investments by an Australian hospital group.

verification_notes: Only source found is a data-aggregator (CB Insights) snippet rather than an official Ramsay or Harrison.ai press release; could not independently corroborate deal terms or confirm Ramsay runs any broader, named venture program beyond this single disclosed investment.

strategy.thesis: I-MED Radiology Network, Australia and New Zealand's largest diagnostic-imaging network, took a minority equity stake in AI-radiology startup Harrison.ai to help develop and deploy AI-assisted imaging tools across its 215+ imaging centres.

summary.en: I-MED Radiology Network is Australia's largest medical-imaging provider (215+ centres across Australia and New Zealand) that took a minority equity stake in AI-radiology startup Harrison.ai; I-MED itself was agreed to be acquired by Jardine Matheson in 2026, with the Harrison.ai stake carried into that transaction.

sources.supports: I-MED's minority interest in Harrison.ai carried into the Jardine Matheson acquisition; network size (215 imaging centres); founded 2000
sources.quote: Founded in 2000, I-Med operates a network of 215 diagnostic imaging centers across Australia and New Zealand, handling about 7 million procedures annually. The transaction also includes I-MED's minority interest in Harrison.ai, a pioneer in developing radiology artificial intelligence solutions.

verification_notes: I-MED was owned by UK private-equity firm Permira and, as of mid-2026, had agreed to be acquired by Jardine Matheson (deal not confirmed closed in sources reviewed); included here as an Australia-headquartered diagnostics operator with its own disclosed strategic startup investment, not as an independent fund manager. No separate 'I-MED Ventures' brand exists.
